howItWorks.title: Four steps to a good round.

rulesPage.title: Rules
rulesPage.subtitle: The "how it works" section covers the app. This is the actual game: "Mensch ärgere Dich nicht", or Ludo.

sections.title: Objective
sections.text: Be the first to move all four of your pieces out of your yard, all the way around the board, and into your own home column.

sections.title: Setup
sections.text: 2 to 4 players each get four pieces in their color, waiting in their yard. The game starts once everyone in the lobby is ready.

sections.title: Rolling and extra turns
sections.text: The server rolls for you automatically at the start of every turn. Rolling a six grants an extra roll right after that turn's move.

sections.title: Leaving the yard and moving
sections.text: A piece needs a six to leave the yard for its starting square. Once out, move the chosen piece forward by the number rolled along the track.

sections.title: Capturing
sections.text: Land exactly on a cell occupied by an opponent's piece to send it back to their yard - it has to start over from there. The same can happen to you, anywhere along the shared track.

sections.title: Winning
sections.text: Once a piece completes the full lap, it turns into your own private home column and is safe from capture. The first player to get all four pieces home wins the round.

variants.title: Move timer
variants.text: When you have more than one legal move, the host-configured timer (15-60s) decides how long you have to pick a piece before the turn passes automatically.

variants.title: Automatic moves
variants.text: If a roll leaves you exactly one legal move, it can be played automatically instead of waiting out the timer - the host can turn this off in the lobby.

variants.title: Fair dice
variants.text: Numbers are balanced to come up regularly over a game, so no one waits forever for the six they need - the order each number appears in still stays random.

variants.title: Must spawn on six
variants.text: An optional rule the host can enable: rolling a six with a piece still waiting forces it out of the yard, instead of also offering to move a piece already on the board.

variants.title: Computer opponents
variants.text: The host can fill free seats with bots. They roll and move on their own, and a game against bots can start with just one human player.

variants.title: Removing inactive players
variants.text: The host can remove a player who has gone quiet at any time, even mid-game, and the turn moves on to the next player. If only one player is left, they win. If the host is away for more than 30 seconds, the host role passes to another player. Anyone in the room can take the role over right away once the host is gone. In the lobby, someone who closes their tab is dropped after about 15 seconds.

sections.title: Operator
paragraphs: This website and the game server behind it are operated by the person named above. Contact them using the details above.

sections.title: Liability for content
paragraphs: As a service provider we are responsible for our own content on these pages under general law. Under §§ 8 to 10 DDG we are not obliged to monitor transmitted or stored third-party information, such as the player names other people enter. If we become aware of a violation of the law, we will remove the content promptly.

sections.title: External links
paragraphs: This site links to external websites, such as the project repository on GitHub. We have no influence over their content and accept no liability for it. The respective provider is always responsible. If we learn of a violation, we will remove the link promptly.

sections.title: Trademarks and independence
paragraphs: Names such as "Mensch ärgere Dich nicht" and "Ludo" are used to describe the kind of game this is and may be trademarks of their respective owners. This is an independent hobby project and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to any of them.

sections.title: Who is responsible
paragraphs: The controller within the meaning of the GDPR is the operator named in the Imprint. You can reach them with the contact details given there, including for any privacy question.

sections.title: The short version
paragraphs: Ludo has no accounts, no ads and no analytics or tracking. You only enter a name that you choose yourself. We do not sell personal data and we do not build profiles.

sections.title: What we process, and why
items: Player name: the name you type (or "Guest") is sent to the game server when you create or join a room. Everyone in the room sees it, and if the room is public, the host's name is shown on the discovery page. Please do not use your real name or other personal data if you would rather not share it.

Game data: room code, seat and color, ready status, room settings, dice rolls and moves. This is needed to run the game and is kept in the server's memory only, not in a database. A room is deleted shortly after its last player leaves (after at most five minutes), and when a rematch replaces it.

Technical data: when you visit the site or connect to a game, your IP address and request data (such as browser and time of the request) are processed by the web server and the connection to the game server, in order to deliver pages, keep the real-time connection running, and protect against abuse. Such data may appear temporarily in server logs.
paragraphs: The legal basis is Art. 6 (1) (b) GDPR, as far as it is needed to provide the game you asked to play, and otherwise Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR, our legitimate interest in operating and securing the service.

sections.title: Cookies and browser storage
paragraphs: Ludo stores the following in your browser. It is only used to provide the features you asked for, and contains no tracking identifiers:
items: Cookie ludo_lng (up to one year): remembers the language you picked.
Local storage ludo-theme: remembers your light, dark or system theme choice.
Local storage ludo-sound: remembers whether you turned the sound effects off.
Session storage ludo-player-name: pre-fills your name. It is cleared when you close the tab.
Session storage ludo-player:<room code>: lets you reclaim your seat after a reload. It is cleared when you leave the room or close the tab.

sections.title: Why there is no cookie banner
paragraphs: The storage above is strictly necessary to provide functions you explicitly use, such as switching the language or theme, or rejoining a room after a reload (§ 25 (2) no. 2 TDDDG). We use no advertising, analytics or other tracking technologies, so there is nothing to ask consent for.

sections.title: Fonts and third parties
paragraphs: Fonts are downloaded when the site is built and served from our own domain, so your browser does not contact Google when you visit. We do not embed third-party scripts, trackers or social media widgets. The GitHub link leaves this site; GitHub's own privacy policy applies once you follow it.

sections.title: Sharing and hosting
paragraphs: The site and game server run on infrastructure operated by the operator. We do not sell or otherwise pass on personal data. Data is only disclosed where the law requires it, for example to authorities.

sections.title: Retention
paragraphs: Game data lives in memory and disappears with the room or when the server restarts. Log data, if any, is kept only as long as needed for security and troubleshooting. Browser storage stays on your device until it expires or you clear it.

sections.title: Your rights
paragraphs: Under the GDPR you have the right of access (Art. 15), rectification (Art. 16), erasure (Art. 17), restriction of processing (Art. 18), data portability (Art. 20) and objection (Art. 21). You can clear your browser storage at any time. Because games are not tied to an account, we may not be able to identify data about you without extra information from you.
You also have the right to lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority.

sections.title: Children
paragraphs: Ludo is not aimed at children and we do not knowingly collect data from them. Please do not enter personal data of others as a player name.

sections.title: Changes
paragraphs: We may update this policy when the service changes. The date at the top shows when it was last updated.

sections.title: Scope
paragraphs: These terms apply to your use of Ludo, a free online version of the board game, operated by the person named in the Imprint. By using the site you agree to them.

sections.title: The service
paragraphs: Ludo is free and needs no account. You can create or join a room, play with others in real time, and add computer opponents. It is a hobby project that keeps changing: features may be added, changed or removed at any time.

sections.title: Fair use
paragraphs: Please play nicely. You agree not to:
items: use names that are offensive, hateful, unlawful, or that impersonate or identify other people;
harass other players or deliberately disrupt games;
cheat, or use bots, scripts or other automation to play, or to bypass the rules or timers;
attack, overload, probe or scrape the site or the game server, or try to get around technical limits;
use the service for anything unlawful.

sections.title: Names and public rooms
paragraphs: You are responsible for the name you enter. Names and room hosts are visible to other people, and to anyone browsing public rooms. Hosts can remove players from their lobby, and we may remove rooms or block access if these terms are broken.

sections.title: Availability
paragraphs: The service is provided "as is" and "as available". We do not promise it will be uninterrupted or error-free. Games run in server memory, so a restart or update can end running games and rooms without notice.

sections.title: Liability
paragraphs: We are fully liable for intent and gross negligence, for injury to life, body or health, and where mandatory law requires it. For slight negligence we are only liable for breach of essential contractual obligations, and then limited to the foreseeable damage typical for this kind of service. Any further liability is excluded, which also applies to the personal liability of employees and agents.

sections.title: Open source
paragraphs: The source code is available in the project repository on GitHub, linked in the footer.

sections.title: Changes to these terms
paragraphs: We may update these terms when the service changes. Continuing to use Ludo after an update means you accept the new version.

sections.title: Governing law
paragraphs: German law applies, excluding the UN Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods. If you are a consumer, mandatory consumer protection rules of the country where you live remain unaffected.
